name: Paraguay
snapshot: President Santiago Peña resigned and was impeached on the same day in November 2026 over the collapse of Ueno Bank, in which he had held shares, and remains in office while the Senate tries him.
culture: Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where most people speak an Indigenous language, Guaraní, which is official alongside Spanish. Tereré, cold yerba mate, is drunk everywhere. The harp and the polka paraguaya are central to its music. The Jesuit missions of the 17th and 18th centuries left UNESCO-listed ruins.
society: Paraguay is a top exporter of soy and beef, and the Itaipú and Yacyretá dams produce more electricity than it uses. Land is very unequally distributed. It is one of the few countries still recognising Taiwan instead of China. Smuggling and money laundering in the tri-border area with Brazil and Argentina are a concern.
situation: Santiago Peña was elected in 2023 with the backing of former president Horacio Cartes, who is under US corruption sanctions, and aligned closely with Washington, Israel and Javier Milei. On 3 November 2026 the central bank seized Ueno Bank, a digital lender with about three million customers and about 380 million dollars of state pension money, owned by Peña's former business partners. On 5 November, after Cartes and the Colorado Party turned on him, Peña announced his resignation, deputies impeached him 78 to 0, and a joint session to accept the resignation failed for lack of a quorum, so he remains president while the Senate tries him. Removal needs 30 of 45 votes; Vice President Pedro Alliana would serve out the term to 2028.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single five-year term; Congress has a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies, both dominated by the Colorado Party.
